conviction_note: The quarter is a modest EPS-beat base case on a name that sold its last two EPS beats on small revenue misses. The print turns on the first FY27 guide including Megger, which closed Oct 1. The street's FY27 bar ($9.22 EPS, $1.72B revenue) is a mix of analysts who include Megger and analysts who do not, so it is disputed. Management's initial guides have been conservative, and my deal arithmetic puts a combined FY27 at roughly $8.95-9.40. Against that, the stock is 23% below its August level, at the post-earnings low and about 30% under the mean target, so expectations are already reset. Strong Navy counterparties lean mildly positive. Those offsets net to about zero (impact_sum +0.1). p_up is 52 and abs_move 8.0 (above the 6.23 median because a first acquisition-inclusive guide is likely and coverage is thin), so the scaled number is +0.32.

Consensus is $2.59-2.60 at Earnings Whispers and Yahoo, $2.62 at Chartmill, with a $2.65 whisper (https://finviz.com/news/421325/escos-fourth-quarter-must-prove-navy-and-test-strength-outrun-nrg-drag-as-stock-slumps). Q4 revenue consensus is $375.4-375.6M (Yahoo, 4 analysts, range $372-382.3M: https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/ESE/analysis); the FY guide of $1.30-1.33B less 9M sales of $938.0M implies $362-395M (midpoint about $378.5M). Both sources agree on the quarter's bar. The FY27 bar is DISPUTED: Yahoo shows FY27 EPS $9.22 (range $8.86-9.51) and revenue $1.72B (range $1.40-2.07B), and the revenue range shows some estimates exclude Megger (about $590M in 2026). So guidance-dependent findings are capped small.

next_guide.basis: This is the first FY27 guide and it includes a $2.3B acquisition. Its initial FY26 guide ($7.50-7.80) ended at $8.30-8.40, a conservative-start habit. The street bar mixes analysts with and without Megger, so the direction against consensus is genuinely uncertain.

findings.finding: Expectations are already reset. The stock is down about 23% since the Aug 6 print (about 20pp behind the S&P) and sits at $226.75, near the $225 post-earnings low, 36% below its 52-week high and roughly 29-46% below the analyst mean ($317.5-385) and high ($420) targets. It trades about 27x FY26 and 24.6x the street's FY27 $9.22, against the 56.6x P/E Simply Wall St cited going into the Aug print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After the -6.8% (Aug) and -8.9% (May) prints the stock kept falling into this one. The last time it entered a print depressed (Feb 2025, after an 11.65% slide noted by AAII) it moved +19.75%. That is one observation, not a pattern.

If the market still held a high bar, the stock would sit near its 200-day (about $288) and targets would not be 30%+ above spot. A depressed entry makes a merely in-line print less likely to be sold hard.

findings.finding: The first FY27 guide includes Megger (closed Oct 1: $922M cash plus 5.10M new shares, about $1.0B borrowed at a stated cost of debt 'around 6%', Megger 2026 revenue about $590M, deal priced at about 14x 2026E EBITDA including $60M of three-year synergies). The street's FY27 EPS of $9.22 ($8.86-9.51) mixes analysts with and without Megger. My arithmetic (standalone about $9.2 on 25.9M shares; Megger EBIT less about $55M of interest, taxed, on about 31M shares) gives a combined $8.95-9.40. With management's habit of conservative initial guides (FY26 started at $7.50-7.80 and ended at $8.30-8.40), the guide midpoint is at real risk of landing at or below $9.22. Management's 'accretive in the first 12 months' claim limits the downside.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Nov 20 2025 initial FY26 guide ($7.50-7.80) drew +2.54% (baseline). In-year guide raises in May and Aug were sold (-8.91%, -6.80%) because revenue missed. There is no prior acquisition-inclusive initial guide in the 8-print history.
findings.why_not_priced: The FY27 consensus range ($1.40B-2.07B revenue) shows some analysts have not modelled Megger, so no clean street number exists for the combined company. EPS revisions turned down slightly (from $9.32 sixty days ago to $9.22, one cut in the last 7 days). If the market were pricing a conservative guide, the cut would be visible across the range rather than in one name.
findings.independence: Deal terms: Apr 15 2026 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000866706/000110465926043869/tm2611891d1_ex99-1.htm, $590M revenue, 14x EBITDA including synergies). Cost of debt and 'Megger up nicely': Aug 6 2026 call transcript (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/ESE/Q32026). Street figures: https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/ESE/analysis. The combined-EPS arithmetic is my inference. FY26 guide history: Aug 6 8-K. The guide timing was restated in the Oct 1 release (https://finviz.com/news/398039/esco-completes-acquisition-of-megger-group-limited); that is the same fact as this finding.

findings.finding: ESCO missed revenue consensus for three straight quarters while beating EPS: Q1 FY26 $309.3M below estimates, Q2 below, Q3 $339.0M vs $341.4M (-0.7%). The stock fell after the last two (-8.91%, -6.80%). Q4 revenue consensus is $375.6M (4 analysts, $372-382.3M) against a guide-implied $362-395M (midpoint about $378.5M), and Q4 carries a known NRG decline.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: A small revenue miss with an EPS beat and FY raise was sold -8.91% (May 7 2026) and -6.80% (Aug 6 2026). Q1 FY26 (Feb 5 2026) also missed revenue and rose +6.17%, so the pattern is two of three.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus ($375.6M) sits slightly below the guide-implied midpoint, so the street is not haircutting Q4 revenue for the miss habit. If the market expected a fourth miss, the revenue consensus would sit near the $362M low end.
findings.independence: Q2 FY26 revenue miss: https://www.barchart.com/story/news/1786725/esco-nyseese-reports-sales-below-analyst-estimates-in-q1-cy2026-earnings-stock-drops. Q4 consensus: https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/ESE/analysis. The NRG Q4 decline is on the Aug 6 call (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/ESE/Q32026).

findings.finding: Q4 EPS is likely to beat. The guide is $2.55-2.65, consensus $2.59-2.62 (Yahoo, Earnings Whispers, Chartmill) and the whisper $2.65. ESCO beat EPS in every FY26 quarter (Q1 $1.91 vs $1.84-1.86; Q3 $2.20 vs $2.12) and raised the FY guide at every call. This is the consensus base case and lands inside the company's own range.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS beats bought +6.17% (Feb 2026) but were sold -8.91% (May) and -6.80% (Aug) when revenue missed. This name has not reliably paid for an EPS beat alone.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced: the whisper already sits at the top of the range. What remains is the size of any beat above $2.65.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers preview (https://finviz.com/news/421325/escos-fourth-quarter-must-prove-navy-and-test-strength-outrun-nrg-drag-as-stock-slumps) and the company guide in the Aug 6 8-K are separate sources that agree.

findings.finding: Navy shipbuilders reporting the same Jul-Sep quarter as ESCO's fiscal Q4 grew fast and raised guidance. GD Marine Systems revenue rose 21.1% to $4.96B on Columbia and Virginia material and labor volume, and Electric Boat took $42.1B for nine Virginia-class and $29.5B for five Columbia-class boats. HII Newport News revenue rose 18.1% on submarine volume, and HII raised its 2026 shipbuilding guide. This points to strong A&D Navy shipments and orders for ESCO's submarine-content businesses (Globe Composite, Maritime), whose follow-on supplier awards would show in Q4 orders and the FY27 A&D guide.
findings.link: ESCO's Globe Composite and Maritime (ex-Ultra Maritime) sell submarine components into Virginia- and Columbia-class boats built by Electric Boat and Newport News. The A&D segment was $168.2M of $339M Q3 sales (49.6%) with a $1.1B backlog. ESCO's own Q1 FY26 release cited Virginia Block VI funding at Globe.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: A&D/Navy strength has been the steady line (Q3 A&D +23%, 30.0% margin). It did not prevent the -6.8% in Aug. Navy order lumpiness ($82M in Q3 FY25 'did not fully repeat') was the call's caveat.
findings.why_not_priced: ESCO has not spoken since Aug 6, before both shipbuilder prints. The stock fell 23% over the same weeks the shipbuilders reported acceleration. Had the market carried the Navy read-through, ESE would not have de-rated with defence suppliers rallying.
findings.independence: HII Q3 2026 release (https://finviz.com/news/411262/hii-reports-third-quarter-2026-results, Oct 29 2026) is a different company and document. The GD contract figures come from its call (https://statementdog.com/analysis/GD/earnings_calls/320972, AI-translated).

findings.finding: Hubbell Utility Solutions (Q3 2026, Oct 27) grew organically only 5% (9% reported). Substation sales came in below prior expectations on capacity-expansion timing and about $15M of meter revenue slipped into Q4. The full-year utility organic guide is 6-7%, and the stock fell about 5.5%. This is a mild caution for ESCO's Utility Solutions (Doble, now combined with Megger), whose test and diagnostic products serve utility substation assets.
findings.link: Same end market and channel: US utility T&D and substation spend. Doble sells substation-asset test and diagnostics to the same utilities that buy Hubbell's substation and T&D products. USG was $100M (29%) of ESCO's Q3 sales. Hubbell is not a direct customer or supplier.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: USG has been the softer segment (Q3 +8%, margin down 130bp on NRG). Doble itself grew 17% with orders +30% in Q3, so the utility test line has outrun utility product peers.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a proxy. Hubbell's own stock absorbed it, and no one has mapped it onto Doble/Megger test demand. Hubbell's note of broad order strength across substation, transmission and distribution cuts the other way, hence the small size.
findings.independence: Proxy only. It runs against Doble's own Q3 order growth of +30% (Aug 6 8-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000866706/000110465926092033/tm2621646d1_ex99-1.htm).

findings.finding: Fortive's Intelligent Operating Solutions segment (which includes Fluke electrical test) grew 9.1% core in Q3 2026 on 'robust demand for professional instrumentation', and Fortive raised its FY EPS guide. This is a mild positive read for electrical test-equipment demand, Megger's core market.
findings.link: Fluke and Megger both sell handheld and portable electrical test instruments (insulation and ground testers) to electricians and utilities. Megger is about $590M of revenue now in ESCO's USG. It is not a customer or supplier relationship, and Fortive does not attribute the growth to Fluke by name.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None. Megger has never been in an ESCO print.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a segment-level peer read, and no one maps Fluke onto Megger's contribution to the FY27 guide. It is small because the link is generic.
findings.independence: On Aug 6 management said Megger was 'up nicely over the prior year' (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/ESE/Q32026).

findings.finding: Management pre-warned that NRG (renewables data and monitoring) will decline year over year again in Q4 after the US renewables tax credits expired, and said it will return to growth only off a lower base in FY27 without regaining FY25 levels. Component and memory-chip inflation was 'not material at this point' but expected. Both are drags on Q4 USG margin and the FY27 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NRG fell 29% in Q3 and cut USG margins 130bp. That print was sold -6.8%, though revenue mix rather than NRG alone drove the move.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced, because management said it. What remains is the size of the FY27 NRG base and any memory-chip cost line in the guide, which the preview flags as the risk to watch.

baseline_tension: No usable options anchor exists. The baseline's -3.6% 5d and -2.7% 20d run-up and 36% drawdown agree with a reset bar, and that leans mildly up against my evidence, which is net flat: guide risk and the revenue-miss habit offset a depressed entry and strong Navy counterparties.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (verify the bar): the Q4 bar is sourced to the company guide plus agreeing estimates, but the FY27 bar is disputed (mixed Megger inclusion), so the next_guide finding is capped smaller (-1.0 to -0.7) and p_up moved 53 to 52.
Lesson 3 (own caveat): the next_guide finding contained its own counter (management's 'accretive in 12 months' claim), so it is resolved into one smaller negative rather than two findings.
Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a reaction): the Q4 EPS-beat finding is cut from +0.3 to +0.2 because this name sold its last two EPS beats.
Lesson 8 (thin coverage): with 4 analysts and a first acquisition-inclusive guide, abs_move_pct stays at 8.0, above the 6.23 median; not cut.
Lessons 5 and 7 left the remaining findings unchanged: the counterparty proxies were already small, and short interest of 3.3% is not crowded.
